—————————

“Aloha Mai Kakou O ʻAnakē Gigi keia, Hula, ‘Ōlelo, ‘Oli, Himeni (Mele)”

Aunty Gigi is a musical force to be reckoned with, specializing in Traditional Hawaiian, Polynesian and island contemporary music. When she’s not strumming her ‘ukulele, guitar, upright bass or electric bass, you’ll find her as a Traditional Hawaiian Cultural Practitioner for Ke Ola Mamo, a Non-Profit Health and Wellness Organization. Aunty Gigi has traveled the world sharing her music and makes it her mission to mentor the next generation in the music industry while sharing the Aloha Spirit wherever she goes.

We look forward to seeing you there!

Tournament Format 

 Everyone plays in every round. 

  • Players will be matched against others with similar records. 
  • No one is eliminated after a loss. 
  • Each round lasts 30 minutes. 
  • Match Points: 
  • Win = 3 points 
  • Tie = 1 point 
  • Loss = 0 points 

After your match is over, report your points to a Judge. The players with the most points at the end of the tournament will be our Tournament Champions!

The Rules

  • Be respectful to all players. 
  • Shake hands, fist bump, or say “Good game” after each match.  
  • Be patient with younger or newer players. 
  • Have fun!
  • Use your own deck or borrow from the library (only one EX/GX/Mega/V card per deck). 
  • Shuffle your deck before each game. 
  • Play to 4 prize cards. 
  • If you need help with a rule, raise your hand for a Judge. Judge decisions are final. 
  • Players will be notified when there are 5 minutes remaining in the match. When time is called the match is over. If no winner is determined, the match is a tie.

events.title: Book Club – Gilead by Marilynne Robinson
events.description:
A New York Times bestseller, Oprah’s Book Club pick, and winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and the National Book Critics Circle Award, Gilead has captivated readers worldwide, with more than one million copies sold. It is also a New York Times Notable Book.

“Quietly powerful [and] moving.” — O, The Oprah Magazine (Recommended Reading)

A profound hymn of praise and lamentation, Gilead explores the God-haunted existence of Reverend John Ames, a man who passionately embraces the beauty, grace, and mysteries of life as he prepares to say goodbye. A deeply moving meditation on faith, love, mortality, and the enduring human spirit, this extraordinary novel invites readers to reflect on the beauty found in life’s simplest moments.

“In 1956, toward the end of Reverend John Ames’s life, he begins a letter to his young son, an account of himself and his forebears. Ames is the son of an Iowan preacher and the grandson of a minister who, as a young man in Maine, saw a vision of Christ bound in chains and came west to Kansas to fight for abolition: He “preached men into the Civil War,” then, at age fifty, became a chaplain in the Union Army, losing his right eye in battle.

Reverend Ames writes to his son about the tension between his father–an ardent pacifist–and his grandfather, whose pistol and bloody shirts, concealed in an army blanket, may be relics from the fight between the abolitionists and those settlers who wanted to vote Kansas into the union as a slave state. And he tells a story of the sacred bonds between fathers and sons, which are tested in his tender and strained relationship with his namesake, John Ames Boughton, his best friend’s wayward son.

This is also the tale of another remarkable vision–not a corporeal vision of God but the vision of life as a wondrously strange creation. It tells how wisdom was forged in Ames’s soul during his solitary life, and how history lives through generations, pervasively present even when betrayed and forgotten.” – Macmillan Publisher’s website

Additional copies of the novel will be available at Kahuku Public and School Library.

—————————

“Aloha Mai Kakou O ʻAnakē Gigi keia, Hula, ‘Ōlelo, ‘Oli, Himeni (Mele)”

Aunty Gigi is a musical force to be reckoned with, specializing in Traditional Hawaiian, Polynesian and island contemporary music. Aunty Gigi has traveled the world sharing her music and makes it her mission to mentor the next generation in the music industry while sharing the Aloha Spirit wherever she goes.

We look forward to seeing you there!
